old: no one coming back down can know how to tell, or can tell at all;
new: no one coming back down knows how to tell, or has the power to;
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "che ridire / né sa né può chi di là sù discende"; the doubled "can … tell" trips aloud.

old: as you ask of the one you give the beloved laurel.
new: as you require before you give your beloved laurel.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "come dimanda dar l'amato alloro" (as the giving of the laurel requires); the relative clause tangled.

old:
into my mind, I made my own,
and fixed my eyes on the sun past all our power —
new:
into my mind, my own act was made,
and I fixed my eyes on the sun past all our custom —
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "il mio si fece, / e fissi li occhi al sole oltre nostr'uso": my act took shape from hers; beyond our custom, not our power.

old: drawn up from there above;
new: drawn back from up there;
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "le luci fissi, di là sù rimote": his eyes removed from the sun above and set on her; the Lectio reversed the direction.

old:
To say in words what it is to pass beyond the human
cannot be done;
new:
To pass beyond the human cannot be told
in words;
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "Trasumanar significar per verba / non si poria": lead with the act itself, as the coinage does.

old: on this body, the Moon, that make
new: on this body, that make
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "questo corpo"; "the Moon" is a gloss in the line.

old:
the outline returning so faint that a pearl
on a white brow comes to the eye
no harder to make out than that —
new:
the outline returning as faint
as a pearl on a white brow
comes to the eye —
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "debili sì, che perla in bianca fronte / non vien men forte a le nostre pupille": the outlines are as faint as a pearl on a white brow; the Lectio's comparison ran backward.

old:
if it is the nature of love
to live here
new:
if living in love
is necessary here
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "s'essere in carità è qui necesse": a condition of being here, not a claim about love's nature.

old:
so that, however we are ranked
from sphere to sphere across this realm,
it pleases the whole realm, as it pleases the King
who draws our will into his own.
new:
so that, however we are ranked from sphere to sphere
across this realm, it pleases all the realm,
as it pleases the King who draws our will into his own.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): a three-line tercet ("sì che, come noi sem di soglia in soglia…"); the Lectio had stretched it to four lines, putting the canto one line over.

old: Not the Seraph most in-Godded of them all,
new: Not the Seraph most deeply drawn into God,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "D'i Serafin colui che più s'india"; the hyphenated coinage trips the ear.

old: of the heaven that stands the lowest of them all.
new: of the rank in heaven that rises least of all.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "de la celestïal c'ha men salita": the lowest degree of glory, not this sphere; Beatrice's point is that they do not live here.

old:
than the words sound — a sense not to be mocked,
and worth more than a quick dismissal grants.
new:
than the words sound, and may well carry
a sense that is not to be mocked.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "ed esser puote / con intenzion da non esser derisa"; the last line was padding.

old:
is a matter for faith to wrestle with — a hard
belief, not a heresy that stains the soul.
new:
is an argument for faith, and not
for heresy and wickedness.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "è argomento di fede e non d'eretica nequizia"; "wrestle with" and "a hard belief" were explanation added to the text.

old: men do under protest
new: men do against their will
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "contra grato"; "under protest" is a legal idiom.

old: I have already spoken with that precision.
new: I spoke with precision a little while ago.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "sì preciso di sopra si favella"; "with that precision" pointed at nothing.

old: Christians, be graver than this in your moves.
new: Christians, be slower and graver in how you move.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "Siate, Cristiani, a muovervi più gravi"; "moves" reads as game or slang.

old: before your campaign of war is laid down —
new: before you have laid your warfare down —
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "anzi che 'l militar s'abbandoni"; "campaign of war" was redundant.

old: After Constantine turned
new: "After Constantine turned
why: The whole canto is Justinian's speech (Longfellow opens and closes it with quotation marks); without them a reader takes it for Dante's narration. Closing mark at seg-0048.

old: that any contradiction is both false and true.
new: that of two contradictory claims, one is false and one true.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "ogne contradizione e falsa e vera": of each contradictory pair one side is false, the other true; in English the literal line asserts a paradox, the opposite of what is meant.

old: with more, so that you see
new: with something more;
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "perché tu veggi" opens the next tercet (31); realigns seg-0010/0011 to the source stanzas.

old:
with how much right men move against
the sacred standard,
new:
so that you see with how much right men move
against the sacred standard,
why: Takes up "so that you see" from seg-0010, as the Italian tercet begins "perché tu veggi".

old: the Isere saw, the Saone, the Seine,
new: the Isère saw, the Saône, the Seine,
why: Diacritics restored.

old: the glory of avenging his own wrath.
new: the glory of avenging its own wrath.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "la gloria di far vendetta a la sua ira": the wrath is the living Justice's (God's), not the third Caesar's.

old:
and when our longings lean and rise toward that,
bent that way,
new:
and when desires climb toward such ends,
swerving so,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "e quando li disiri poggian quivi, / sì disvïando"; "lean and rise … bent that way" doubled and blurred the image.

old: of what we earn against what we deserved,
new: of our wages against what we deserved,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "commensurar d'i nostri gaggi / col merto"; "earn" and "deserved" said the same thing, so the comparison vanished.

old: But the Provencals
new: But the Provençals
why: Diacritic restored.

old: it would praise him more.
new: it would praise him more."
why: Closes Justinian's speech opened at seg-0001.

old:
"Osanna sanctus Deus Sabaòth,
 shining above with the brightness of your light
 on the happy fires of these kingdoms!"
new:
"Osanna, sanctus Deus sabaòth,
superillustrans claritate tua
felices ignes horum malacòth!"
why: Latin policy: Dante's three Latin lines stay in Latin with no in-line English (Longfellow keeps them too); the Lectio had turned lines 2-3 into English.

old:
note this with care,
 and the finest reasoning —
new:
if you weigh this
with your finest care —
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "se tu badi / ben con ogne sottigliezza"; the aside had lost its verb.

old:
Between the first day and the final night
 there never was, and never will there be,
 a deed so high and magnificent as this,
why: Realign, Par. VII 112-114 ("o per l'una o per l'altra, fu o fie"): the tercet had spilled its last phrase into seg-0039.

old:
by the one road or by the other — for God,
 in giving his own self, was more openhanded
 toward making man able to lift himself again
why: Realign, Par. VII 115-117 ("ché più largo fu Dio … che s'elli avesse sol da sé dimesso").

new:
and every other way fell short of justice,
unless the Son of God had humbled himself
to take on flesh and be born into the world.
why: Realign, Par. VII 118-120 ("… non fosse umilïato ad incarnarsi").

old:
to take on flesh and be born into the world.
 Now, to fill every desire of yours completely,
 I will go back and make one point as clear
new:
Now, to fill every desire of yours completely,
I will go back and make one point
as clear to you as it is to me.
why: Realign, Par. VII 121-123 ("perché tu veggi lì così com' io").

old:
to you as it is to me. You are saying: 'I see
 the air, I see the fire, the water and the earth,
 and all that is mixed from them, come to ruin
why: Realign, Par. VII 124-126 ("venire a corruzione, e durar poco").

old:
and last only a little while — and yet
 these things were created.' And so, you reason,
 if what I said is true, they too should stand
 secure against corruption, and not decay.
new:
and yet these things were created.' And so, you reason,
if what I said is true, they too should stand
secure against corruption, and not decay.
why: Realign, Par. VII 127-129; the segment had run to four lines. With seg-0038-0042 the canto is back to the source's 148 lines.

old:
so the ancient peoples in their ancient error
gave her not only the honor of their cries
and sacrifices, but worshipped Dione too
why: Realign, Par. VIII 4-6 ("le genti antiche ne l'antico errore"): Dione belongs to the next tercet.
Realign, Par. VIII 7-9 ("ma Dïone onoravano e Cupido…").

old:
they took the name they gave the planet's light
that courts the sun, sometimes behind it, trailing,
and sometimes running on before its face.
new:
and from her, with whom I now begin, they took the name
of the planet's light that courts the sun,
sometimes trailing behind it, sometimes running on before its face.
why: Realign, Par. VIII 10-12 ("e da costei ond' io principio piglio / pigliavano il vocabol de la stella"); drops the gloss "Venus", which Dante leaves as "costei".

old:
Already the crown of that land flashed upon
my brow whose waters are the Danube's, once
new:
Already on my brow there flashed the crown
of the land the Danube waters, once
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "Fulgeami già in fronte la corona / di quella terra che 'l Danubio riga"; the relative clause had attached to "my brow".

old:
And he again: "Now tell me — would it be
worse for a man on earth if he lived
as no part of a city?" "Yes," I said,
new:
And he again: "Now tell me — would it be worse
for a man on earth if he lived as no part of a city?"
"Yes," I said, "and here I ask no reason why."
why: Realign, Par. VIII 115-117 ("'Sì,' rispuos' io; 'e qui ragion non cheggio'"): from here to the end each segment carried the head of the next tercet.

new:
"And can he be one, unless men live below
in different ways, for offices that differ?
No — not if your own master writes it true."
why: Realign, Par. VIII 118-120; also keeps "No, if your master writes it well" inside Charles's speech ("Non, se 'l maestro vostro ben vi scrive" is his own answer), where the old quote break made it read as Dante's.

old:
"No — not if your own master writes it true."
So step by step his reasoning arrived,
and then he closed: "It follows, then, that the roots
new:
So step by step his reasoning arrived,
and then he closed: "It follows, then, that the roots
of what you each become must be diverse:
why: Realign, Par. VIII 121-123 ("convien di vostri effetti le radici").

old:
of what you each become must be diverse:
one man is born a Solon, one a Xerxes,
one a Melchizedek, and one the man
new:
so one man is born a Solon, one a Xerxes,
one a Melchizedek, and one the man
who flew through the air and lost his son in falling.
why: Realign, Par. VIII 124-126; the tercet had ended mid-name.

old:
who flew through the air and lost his son in falling.
The wheeling heavens, a seal pressed into mortal wax,
practice their art and practice it with skill,
why: Realign, Par. VIII 127-129; also "ch'è suggello / a la cera mortal": the heavens are the seal, not something pressed into the wax.

new:
so it comes about that Esau differs
in the seed from Jacob, and Quirinus springs
from a father so base he is given to Mars.
why: Realign, Par. VIII 130-132.

old:
from a father so base he is given to Mars.
A nature, once begotten, would always run
the road its parents ran before it, if
new:
A nature, once begotten, would always run
the road its parents ran before it, if
the providence of God did not prevail.
why: Realign, Par. VIII 133-135.
Realign, Par. VIII 136-138.

old:
in you, I'll wrap you in a corollary:
always, if a nature meets a fortune
out of tune with it — like any seed
new:
always, when a nature meets a fortune
out of tune with it, like any seed
far from its native ground, it comes to no good.
why: Realign, Par. VIII 139-141 ("fuor di sua regïon, fa mala prova").

old:
dropped far outside its native ground — it thrives
to no good purpose; and if the world below
would only fix its mind on the foundation
new:
And if the world below would only fix its mind
on the foundation nature lays,
and follow that, its people would be good.
why: Realign, Par. VIII 142-144.

old:
that nature lays, and follow that, its people
would be good. But you wrench toward the cloister
one born to buckle on the sword, and crown
why: Realign, Par. VIII 145-147 ("e fate re di tal ch'è da sermone"); "crown … king" had been split across a line and a segment.

old:
a man fit only for the pulpit king;
and so the track you walk runs off the road."
new: and so the track you walk runs off the road."
why: Closing-line policy: Par. VIII 148 stands alone, as in the source; the canto is back to 148 lines.

old: will stain red the water
new: will change the water
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "Padova al palude / cangerà l'acqua che Vicenza bagna"; "red" spells out what Dante leaves implied.

old:
Up here, gladness is gained as added brightness,
the way down there it shows as a smile;
but in the dark below, the shade grows black
as the mind inside it darkens with its grief.
new:
Up here, gladness is gained as brightness,
as down there it shows as a smile; but below,
the shade grows dark outside as the mind grows sad.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "Per letiziar là sù fulgor s'acquista, / sì come riso qui; ma giù s'abbuia / l'ombra di fuor, come la mente è trista": a tercet the Lectio had stretched to four lines with added matter.

old: as long as it became these graying locks —
new: as long as it still became my youthful hair —
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "infin che si convenne al pelo": while it suited his age, i.e. in youth; "graying" says the opposite.

old:
Into this heaven, where the cone of shadow
cast by your world comes to its point and ends,
she was raised up before all other souls,
the first that Christ's great triumph carried off.
new:
Into this heaven, where the cone of shadow
cast by your world comes to its point, she was raised
first of all the souls of Christ's triumph.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "pria ch'altr' alma / del trïunfo di Cristo fu assunta": a tercet stretched to four lines, the last repeating "before all other souls". With seg-0024 the canto is back to 142 lines.

old: this whoring of the faith.
new: this adultery.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "de l'avoltero": adultery, the Church as bride betrayed; "whoring" is coarser and shifts the figure.

old:
I cannot tell, though I call on every gift
of genius, art, and practice — only believe
that it can be, and ache to see it for yourself.
new:
I could not tell it so that it could be imagined,
though I call on genius, art, and practice — but believe it,
and ache to see it for yourself.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "Perch' io lo 'ngegno e l'arte e l'uso chiami, / sì nol direi che mai s'imaginasse; / ma creder puossi": the Lectio had dropped "so that it could be imagined".

old:
where no one comes back down
without first climbing it again,
new:
where no one comes back down
who will not climb it again,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "u' sanza risalir nessun discende": whoever comes down will climb again; "first" reversed the order.

old:
was Peter — Peter the Lombard, who like
the poor widow gave
new:
was that Peter who, like
the poor widow, gave
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "quel Pietro fu che con la poverella"; "the Lombard" is a gloss.

old: you want me to unpack
new: you want me to sift again
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "ricerna" (sift again); "unpack" is current idiom.

old: 'where the sheep grow fat,'
new: 'where a man grows fat,'
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "u' ben s'impingua" in both X and XI; Canto X here reads "where a man / grows fat", so Thomas's self-quotation must match it (see seg-0047).

old: but Orient,
new: but the East,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "Oriente": the sunrise quarter; "Orient" now reads as dated or loaded.

old: first kicked his shoes off and ran
new: first went barefoot and ran
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "si scalzò": bared his feet as a friar does; "kicked his shoes off" suggests lounging.

old: 'where the sheep grow fat, if they do not stray.'
new: 'where a man grows fat, if he does not stray.'
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "u' ben s'impingua, se non si vaneggia", quoting Canto X, where the Lectio has "where a man / grows fat … if only he does not stray".

old:
O his father, Felix — "happy" indeed!
O his mother, Joanna — "grace of God" —
new:
O his father, truly Felix!
O his mother, truly Joanna,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "Oh padre suo veramente Felice! / oh madre sua veramente Giovanna"; the meanings of the names were glosses in the line, and the nested double quotes clashed with the speech's own.

old: following Ostian law and Taddeo's medicine,
new: following the man of Ostia and Taddeo,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "di retro ad Ostïense e a Taddeo": two men, the canonist and the physician; "Ostian law" and "medicine" were glosses.

old: no tithes that belong to God's poor;
new: non decimas, quae sunt pauperum Dei;
why: Latin policy: Dante writes "non decimas, quae sunt pauperum Dei" in Latin (Longfellow keeps it).

old:
But the track laid down by the rim of that wheel,
at its very best, is abandoned now:
new:
But the track cut by the topmost part
of that wheel's rim is abandoned now:
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "Ma l'orbita che fé la parte somma / di sua circunferenza, è derelitta"; "at its very best" has no source.

old: always set the sinister concerns aside.
new: always put worldly concerns last.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "posposi sempre la sinistra cura": the left-hand, worldly care; a reader today hears "sinister" as evil.

old: and Peter the Eater,
new: and Peter Comestor,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "Pietro Mangiadore" (Comestor); translating the epithet makes a proper name comic.

old: nor from the Love bound into them,
new: nor from the Love that makes them Three,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "né da l'amor ch'a lor s'intrea": the Love that makes a third with them; "bound into" lost the Trinity.

old: draws its own rays back through its goodness
new: through its own goodness gathers its rays
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "per sua bontate il suo raggiare aduna": gathers; "draws back" suggests withdrawal.

old: who set out and knew not where;
new: who set out not knowing where;
why: Leftover archaism "knew not".

old: gave up its speaking — for what came next
new: gave up its speaking;
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "per la similitudine che nacque" opens the next tercet (13); realigns seg-0002/0003.

old: carried the same likeness, passing from his words
new: for the same likeness carried on, passing from his words
why: Takes up the causal clause from seg-0002, as the Italian tercet begins "per la similitudine".

old: is as much grace as it has earned beyond its worth.
new: as great as the grace it is given beyond its worth.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "e quella tanta, / quant' ha di grazia sovra suo valore": grace beyond merit; "earned" contradicted "beyond its worth".

old:
appeared to me — and she must be left out
from among the sights my memory could not keep.
new:
appeared to me, that I must leave her
among the sights my memory could not keep.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "che tra quelle vedute si vuol lasciar / che non seguir la mente": he leaves her among those sights; "left out from among" excluded her from them.

old: borne up to higher rescue,
new: borne up to higher blessedness,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "a più alta salute": blessedness, not rescue.

old: more red than it was wont.
new: redder than before.
why: Leftover archaism "wont".

old: flashed Christ, like lightning gone,
new: Christ flashed out like lightning,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "quella croce lampeggiava Cristo"; "like lightning gone" is unclear.

old:
drift across the sunbeam that streaks the dark
people rig for their own shade — the shaft of light
they contrive against the glare with craft and art.
new:
drift across the sunbeam that sometimes streaks the shade
that people, to defend themselves,
contrive with craft and art.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "per lo raggio onde si lista / talvolta l'ombra che, per sua difesa, / la gente con ingegno e arte acquista"; across the line break "the dark / people" read aloud as one phrase.

old: at the first slip Guinevere set down in writing.
new: at the first slip of Guinevere's the old tale records.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "al primo fallo scritto di Ginevra": the fault written of Guinevere; the Lectio made her the writer.

old: "From the day the angel said 'Hail' to the birth
new: "From the day 'Ave' was spoken to the birth
why: Latin policy: "Da quel dì che fu detto 'Ave'"; Dante's Latin word stays (Longfellow keeps it), and "the angel" was a gloss.

old: it will soon throw the ship overboard,
new: it will soon be thrown from the ship,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "che tosto fia iattura de la barca": the load will be jettisoned; the ship is not thrown overboard.

old: its teeth or his purse
new: his teeth or his purse
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "a chi mostra 'l dente / o ver la borsa": the man shows his teeth, not the breed.

old: with a gold border
new: with a border
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "fascia col fregio": no metal named; "gold" is a gloss.

old: no triangle can hold two right angles wide,
new: no triangle can hold two obtuse angles,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "non capere in trïangol due ottusi".

old:
that was wronged, in the loud public cry —
but the truth that deals out vengeance will bear witness.
new:
that was wronged, in the loud public cry; but the vengeance
will bear witness to the truth that deals it out.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "ma la vendetta / fia testimonio al ver che la dispensa": subject and object were swapped.

old: you are thrown among into this valley;
new: you will fall with into this valley;
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "con la qual tu cadrai in questa valle"; "among into" is ungrammatical.

old: will, yes, find your words harsh.
new: will surely find your words harsh.
why: "yes" is filler.
Latin policy: the skywritten Latin stays as Dante wrote it, without the in-line English glosses.

old: But you, who write only to cancel it out —
new: But you, who write only so you can cancel —
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "Ma tu che sol per cancellare scrivi"; "it" had no antecedent.

old: though they do not follow the story.
new: though they do not follow its example.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "ma non seguon la storia": they do not carry on its example; "the story" is ambiguous in English.

old: to those who joy up there.
new: to those who rejoice up there.
why: "joy" as a verb is archaic.

old:
And let everyone believe that even now,
as first installment of it, Nicosia
and Famagosta wail and rage
new:
And let everyone believe that even now,
as first installment, Nicosia and Famagosta
wail and rage because of their own beast,
why: Realign, Par. XIX 145-147 ("per la lor bestia si lamenti e garra"): the tercet had spilled into the closing line.

old:
because of their own beast, who keeps
in step, and never strays from the others' flank."
new: who never strays from the others' flank."
why: Closing-line policy: Par. XIX 148 ("che dal fianco de l'altre non si scosta") stands alone as one line; "keeps in step" was padding.

old: "now you must hold your gaze on, hard,
new: "is what you must now look at steadily,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "or fisamente riguardar si vole"; the stranded preposition tripped the line.

old: so the song takes on more delight —
new: and the song takes on more delight from it —
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "in che più di piacer lo canto acquista"; the "so" collided with the "so" opening the next tercet.

old:
moving their small flames
to the words.
new: moving their small flames in time to the words.
why: Closing-line policy: Par. XX 148 is one line, not two.

old:
would see how glad I was to obey
my guide from heaven — once he weighed
the one side of the balance against the other.
new:
would know, weighing the one side against the other,
how glad I was to obey
my guide from heaven.
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "conoscerebbe quanto m'era a grato / ubidire a la mia celeste scorta, / contrapesando l'un con l'altro lato": the weigher is the reader; placed after "my guide", "he weighed" read as the guide and made Beatrice male.

old: that nothing here could match it — and I
new: that nothing here could match it; nor could I
why: Closing-line policy: prepares Par. XXI 142 to stand as one whole line.

old:
could make nothing of it, the thunder so
overwhelmed me.
new: make it out, the thunder so overwhelmed me.
why: Closing-line policy: Par. XXI 142 ("lo tuon m'avvinse") as one line, not split mid-phrase.

old: that heaven is wholly holy,
new: that all of heaven is holy,
why: Italian (from my own knowledge, not bundled): "il cielo è tutto santo"; the jingle drew attention to itself.

old: the longing I held back about itself.
